content.value:
InstantCommand runs an action once and finishes immediately. It's the simplest command.

You pass it a Runnable lambda — a block of code wrapped in () -> { ... }.

Declare a private DcMotor field.

In initialize(), get "front_left_motor" from hardwareMap.

You've done this many times — type it from memory.

steps.title: Schedule an InstantCommand to start the motor

content.value:
In initialize(), write:

schedule(new InstantCommand(() -> motor.setPower(0.5)));

Add a second schedule() call with another InstantCommand that sets motor power to 0.0.

Both commands run at the same time — the first starts the motor, the second stops it.

InstantCommand finishes so fast the motor won't move. Later you'll learn commands that control timing and duration.

A command can require a subsystem by passing it as a parameter after the lambda:

schedule(new InstantCommand(() -> motor.setPower(0.5), driveSubsystem));

Requiring a subsystem tells the scheduler this command uses that subsystem. Only one command may require a given subsystem at a time — if another command needs it, the scheduler interrupts this one.

You can pass several subsystems after the lambda. Subsystems themselves are covered in the next lesson.

steps.title: What you can do with InstantCommand

content.value:
InstantCommand is one of many built-in command types.

SolversLib also provides ConditionalCommand (runs one of two commands based on a condition), ProxyCommand (defers command creation until scheduled), and others.

The next few lessons cover WaitCommand, WaitUntilCommand, RunCommand, and the group containers — but there's more beyond that. Please read the documentation after you finish all the lessons.
